title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 2 diabetes and recent hypoglycemic episode.

HPI
The patient is a 62-year-old individual presenting for a scheduled follow-up regarding their diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient reports that they have been managed on a long-term regimen of insulin and an oral hypoglycemic agent. They report experiencing a hypoglycemic episode two days ago, characterized by sudden sweating and tremors. The patient states they were able to resolve the symptoms by consuming a fast-acting carbohydrate. They continue to monitor their blood glucose levels daily.

Medication List
- Insulin (long-term)
- Metformin (long-term)

Exam
The patient appears in no acute distress. They are alert and oriented. Vital signs are stable. Physical examination of the skin and extremities shows no acute findings.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
2. Hypoglycemia

Plan
The patient will continue the current regimen of insulin and metformin. We discussed the importance of monitoring for symptoms of a hypoglycemic episode and the necessity of carrying a source of glucose at all times. The patient will return in four weeks for a follow-up.
explanations: Diabetes with hypoglycemia and no coma documented: E11.649.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Hypoglycemia is a complication with its own code.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
